summary: Stocks fell midday Wednesday after a hot inflation report revived talk of a Fed rate hike. Tech led the slide, with chips and megacaps taking the worst of it.
market_note: S&P 500 off about 1.3%, Nasdaq down over 2%; VIX jumped roughly 12%.

items.why: Hot CPI made rate-sensitive chip names the hardest hit. AMD's pricey valuation and its OpenAI revenue ties left little room for optimism, and Monday's Helion rack news failed to excite.
Sold off with the AI-chip complex as the hot inflation print put another Fed hike back in play. Reuters noted chipmakers leading the Nasdaq lower as bank earnings rolled in.
Goldman Sachs cut its price target over rising operating expenses tied to AI spending, while investors de-risk ahead of Q3 earnings on October 21.
Dropped as the hot inflation report hammered growth stocks. Barron's noted investors digesting self-driving news, with the trillion-dollar robo-taxi valuation debate back in focus.
